万里长城

THE GREAT WALL

沿着山脊，读懂中国两千多年的历史。Across the mountain ridges, discover more than two thousand years of Chinese history.

EXPLORE ↓
CHAPTER 01 / 08

长城是什么？

What Is the Great Wall?

长城不是一堵从头到尾完全相连的墙，而是不同时代修建的城墙、关口和烽火台组成的防御体系。它跨越山地、草原和沙漠。The Great Wall is not one continuous wall. It is a system of walls, passes and signal towers built in different periods, crossing mountains, grasslands and deserts.

观察：为什么城墙常建在山脊上？Look: Why were walls often built along mountain ridges?
CHAPTER 02 / 08

两千多年的故事

A Story Across Centuries

中国古代许多国家和朝代都修过长城。秦朝连接了一些较早的城墙；今天人们常见的砖石长城，大多来自明朝（1368—1644年）。Many ancient Chinese states and dynasties built defensive walls. The Qin linked some earlier sections. Many of the familiar brick-and-stone sections date to the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).

思考：长城为什么会不断修建和改变？Think: Why was the Wall rebuilt and changed over time?
CHAPTER 03 / 08

长城为什么建？

Why Was It Built?

长城的重要作用是帮助防守边境。城墙、关口和驻军一起控制交通，烽火台可以传递警报。长城也见证了不同地区的人们之间的交流。Its main purpose was frontier defense. Walls, passes and garrisons helped control movement, while signal towers sent warnings. The Wall also witnessed contact and exchange between communities.

想一想：城墙能做什么？又不能做什么？Think: What could a wall do—and what could it not do?
CHAPTER 04 / 08

城墙上的秘密

Anatomy of the Wall

在一些明长城地段，可以看到城墙顶部的道路、两侧的垛口、供士兵观察的敌楼，以及重要的关口。不同地形的建筑样式并不一样。At some Ming-era sections you can see a walkway, protective battlements, watchtowers and fortified passes. The design changes with the landscape.

找一找：照片中哪里是敌楼？Find it: Can you spot a watchtower in the photo?
CHAPTER 05 / 08

山海关到嘉峪关

Across Northern China

山海关靠近渤海，嘉峪关位于甘肃西部，两者都是著名的长城关口。不过，长城遗址远不止两地之间的一条直线，还包括许多支线和不同时期的遗存。Shanhaiguan near the Bohai Sea and Jiayuguan in western Gansu are famous passes. But the Great Wall is much more than a single line between them: it includes branches and remains from different eras.

观察：长城会经过哪些自然环境？Look: What kinds of landscapes does the Wall cross?
CHAPTER 06 / 08

用什么建成？

How Was It Built?

修建长城会使用当地容易获得的材料：有的地方用夯土，有的地方用石块或砖。山地施工十分困难，修建与维护需要大量人力。Builders used materials available locally, including rammed earth, stone and brick. Building in the mountains was difficult and required substantial labor and maintenance.

想一想：沙漠地区为什么不一定用砖？Think: Why might builders in deserts use materials other than brick?
CHAPTER 07 / 08

世界文化遗产

A World Heritage Site

长城于1987年列入联合国教科文组织《世界遗产名录》。它具有重要的历史、建筑和文化价值，也提醒我们尊重古代劳动者的付出。The Great Wall was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1987. It is valued for its history, architecture and culture—and reminds us of the labor behind its construction.

知识点：世界遗产需要大家共同保护。Remember: World Heritage needs protection.
CHAPTER 08 / 08

今天的长城

The Wall Today

八达岭、慕田峪、金山岭等地段吸引许多游客。与此同时，一些较偏远的遗址受到风雨侵蚀和人为损坏。参观时不要刻字，也不要攀爬未开放区域。Sections such as Badaling, Mutianyu and Jinshanling welcome visitors. Other remains face erosion and damage. Visitors should not carve on the stones or enter closed areas.

你会怎样保护一处古老建筑？How would you protect a historic place?

DISCOVERY QUIZ · 知识测试

你了解长城吗？How Well Do You Know the Wall?

1. 长城只是一堵完全相连的墙吗？Is the Great Wall one continuous wall?

2. 今天常见的砖石长城多来自哪个朝代？Many familiar brick-and-stone sections date to which dynasty?

3. 烽火台的重要作用是什么？What was an important role of signal towers?

4. 长城在哪一年列入世界遗产名录？In which year was the Wall inscribed as World Heritage?

5. 长城所有地方都只用砖建成吗？Was every part of the Wall built only from brick?

6. 参观长城时应该怎样做？What should visitors do?
